title: VTT to SRT Converter (Free, In Your Browser)
metaDescription: Convert WebVTT subtitles to SRT for free, in your browser. Paste the text or drop a .vtt file; nothing is uploaded and no account is needed.
intro: Turn a WebVTT (.vtt) file into SubRip (.srt) for editors, players and platforms that expect SRT. Drop the file or paste its text: it's converted on your device and never uploaded.
summary: Turn WebVTT into .srt subtitles, on your device, without an account.

formats.heading: WebVTT
paragraphs: WebVTT (.vtt) starts with a WEBVTT line and can hold more than captions: notes, styling blocks, regions and per-cue settings such as position and alignment. Times use a dot, and the hours are optional (01:02.345).

formats.heading: SRT
paragraphs: SubRip (.srt) is simpler and more widely accepted: numbered cues, full times with a comma (00:01:02,345), and the text. Most video editors and players read it.

formats.heading: What the converter changes
paragraphs: It drops the WEBVTT header, NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks, cue ids and cue settings, writes every time in full with a comma, and numbers the cues from 1. The text of each cue, line breaks included, stays as it was.

faq.question: Is anything uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The converter runs in your browser: the .vtt file is read on your device and the .srt file is created there.

faq.question: What happens to positioning and styling?
faq.answer: SRT has no equivalent for WebVTT's cue settings, STYLE blocks or regions, so they're removed. The timing and the text are kept.

faq.question: Why does it say my file isn't WebVTT?
faq.answer: A WebVTT file must start with a WEBVTT line. If yours starts with a number and a time like 00:00:01,000, it's already an SRT file; use the SRT to VTT converter to go the other way.

faq.question: Are formatting tags kept?
faq.answer: Yes. Text is copied as it is, tags included. SRT players understand simple ones like <i> and <b>; others may show WebVTT-only tags as plain text.

cta.heading: Want captions viewers can't switch off?
cta.text: Supertitle burns captions into the video itself, so they show on every player, platform and phone.
